<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="Hftf" /></noinclude><section begin="par130" />Cf. also {{GHGheb|text=מִיּוֹם א׳}} followed by a {{GHGterm|perfect}} in {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=29|verse=8}}, and {{GHGheb|text=יְמֵי א׳}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Lv|chapter=13|verse=46}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=9|verse=18}}.<ref>In {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=23|verse=5}} the construct state governs a sentence introduced by the ''conjunction'' {{GHGheb|text=אֲשֶׁר}} ({{GHGheb|text=עַל־דְּבַר אֲשֶׁר|translate=by reason of the fact that}}, i.e. ''because''); so also in {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=3|verse=13}}.</ref>

{{GHGmargin-letter|130|d}}
(4) When it governs independent sentences (cf. § 155), which virtually stand to the construct state (as nomen regens) in a sort of genitive relation, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=4|verse=13}} {{GHGheb|text=בְּיַד־תְּשְׁלָח}}<ref>{{GHGcritic|Should be תִּשְׁלָח?}}</ref> prop. ''by the hand of'' him whom ''thou wilt send''; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=23|verse=3}} {{GHGheb|text=דְּבַר מַה־יַּרְאֵ֫נִי|translate=the matter of}} that ''which he shall show me'', i.e. whatever he shall; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=29|verse=1}} {{GHGheb|text=קִרְיַת חָנָה דָוִד|translate=the city where David encamped}}; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=48|verse=36}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=16|verse=3}} (if the text be right), 65:5 ({{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=8|verse=32}}), {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=81|verse=6}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=18|verse=21}} ''the place of him that knoweth not God''; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=29|verse=16}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=La|chapter=1|verse=14}} (if the text be right) ''into the hands'' of those against whom ''I cannot stand''.<ref>Probably {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=22|verse=14}} is also to be so explained (contrary to the accents), and certainly (contrary to the very unnatural division of the verses) {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 Ch|chapter=30|verse=18}}, which should read on thus: {{GHGheb|text=יְהֹוָה הַטּוֹב יְכַפֵּר בְּעַד כָּל־לְבָבוֹ הֵכִין|translate=the good Lord pardon every one that setteth his heart to seek God}}. [See Wickes’ ''Accentuation of the Twenty-one Prose Books of the Old Testament'', p. 140.]</ref> In {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=39|verse=4}} ({{GHGheb|text=כָּל־יֶשׁ־לוֹ}}) the {{GHGheb|text=כָּל־}} takes after it a noun-clause, and in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=9|verse=4}}, still more boldly, a subst. with {{GHGheb|text=לְ}}.—Very often a ''time-determination'' governs the following sentence in this way; thus {{GHGheb|text=אַֽחֲרֵי}} followed by a perfect, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Lv|chapter=25|verse=48}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=5|verse=9}}; {{GHGheb|text=בְּיוֹם}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=102|verse=3}} (before a noun-clause), {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=6|verse=28}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=3|verse=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=4|verse=15}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=22|verse=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=18|verse=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=59|verse=17|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=138|verse=3|hidebook=1}} (in every case before a following perfect), {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=56|verse=10}} (before an imperfect); {{GHGheb|text=מִיּוֹם}} followed by the perfect, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=36|verse=2}}; {{GHGheb|text=כָּל־יְמֵי}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Lv|chapter=14|verse=46}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=25|verse=15}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=29|verse=2}} ({{GHGheb|text=כִּימֵי|translate=as in the days when}}...<ref>Cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Na|chapter=2|verse=9}} {{GHGheb|text=מִימֵי הִיא}}, usually explained to mean ''from the days'' that ''she'' hath been, but the text is evidently very corrupt.</ref>; cf. {{GHGheb|text=כִּימוֹת}} and {{GHGheb|text=שְׁנוֹת}} before a perfect, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=90|verse=15}}); {{GHGheb|text=בְּעֵת}} before a perfect, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=6|verse=15}} (cf. 49:8, 50:31); before an imperfect, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=6|verse=17}}; {{GHGheb|text=תְּחִלַּת}} before a perfect {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ho|chapter=1|verse=2}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|130|e}}
(5) Connected with a following word in apposition; certainly so in such cases as {{GHGheb|text=בְּתוּלַת בַּת־צִיּוֹן|translate=the virgin, the daughter of Zion}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=37|verse=22}}; cf. 23:12, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=14|verse=17}}; also {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=28|verse=7}} {{GHGheb|text=אֵ֫שֶׁת בַּֽעֲלַת־אוֹב|translate=a woman, possessor of a soothsaying spirit}}; cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=21|verse=11}}.—{{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=14|verse=10}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=19|verse=22}} (but read probably {{GHGheb|text=אֲנָשִׁים}} with Moore, as in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=13|verse=14}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=20|verse=13}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=21|verse=10}}); {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=10|verse=6}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=17|verse=13|hidebook=1}} {{GHGterm|Q<sup>e</sup>rê}}; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=46|verse=9}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=35|verse=16}} (?), 78:9, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=20|verse=17}} ''b'' (unless {{GHGheb|text=נַֽהֲרֵי}} or {{GHGheb|text=נַֽהֲלֵי}} be a gloss).

{{GHGmargin-letter|130|f}}
Rem. Some of the above passages may also be explained by supposing that there exists a real genitive relation towards the preceding construct state, which has been, as it were, provisionally left ''in suspenso'', in consequence of the insertion of some interrupting word, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=37|verse=22}}, &c.; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=20|verse=17}} ''a''. Elsewhere ({{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=33|verse=19}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=68|verse=34}}) the {{GHGterm|nomen regens}} probably governs the following construct state directly.<ref>So also {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=28|verse=16}} ''a corner stone of the preciousness'' ({{GHGheb|text=יִקְרַת}} is a ''substantive'' not an ''adjective'') ''of a fixed foundation'', i.e. a precious corner stone of surest foundation.—In {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=20|verse=19}} the text is wholly corrupt; in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=119|verse=128}} read {{GHGheb|text=כָּל־פִּקּוּדֶ֫יךָ}}.</ref>
